items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: Your sugar rose about 11.1 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL). A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: You didn't have any dinners that started at 8 pm or later, which is good because sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. Keep having dinner before 8 pm to see how it affects your sugar.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 13.0 hours of overnight fasting, and 42.9% of nights reached 13 hours. Having an overnight fast is part of your routine, and it's something to continue as you see how it affects your sugar.
